question: A 58-year-old man presents with fatigue. His CBC shows: Hb 9.2 g/dL, MCV 72 fL, MCH 24 pg, platelets 420 × 10⁹/L, WBC 8.4 × 10⁹/L. Which diagnosis must be ACTIVELY EXCLUDED before attributing this to simple iron deficiency?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hypothyroidism causes normocytic or macrocytic anaemia, not microcytic anaemia, and should not be the first concern here.

Correct. Microcytic hypochromic anaemia in a male over 40 (or any post-menopausal woman) must prompt exclusion of GI malignancy — particularly colorectal cancer — as occult GI blood loss. Investigate with faecal occult blood test and colonoscopy before labelling it 'dietary iron deficiency'.
Thalassaemia trait is a possibility but is a lifelong condition. A new presentation of microcytic anaemia in a 58-year-old male requires exclusion of GI malignancy first.
B12 deficiency causes macrocytic anaemia (elevated MCV), not microcytic anaemia.

overallFeedback.feedback: In a male over 40 with new microcytic anaemia, GI malignancy must be excluded. Iron deficiency from dietary lack is a diagnosis of exclusion, not of first resort, in this age group.
Well done. New microcytic anaemia in a male ≥40 years = colorectal cancer until proven otherwise. Always investigate the source of blood loss before attributing it to diet.
